nodes.title: Print Concepts
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can hold a book right-side up, track print left-to-right and top-to-bottom, and point to individual words while reading.

nodes.title: Phonological Awareness
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can identify rhyming words, count syllables, and blend and segment spoken words into onsets and rimes.

nodes.title: Phonemic Awareness
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can isolate, blend, and segment individual phonemes in spoken one-syllable words.

nodes.title: Letter Recognition
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can name all 26 upper- and lower-case letters and produce their most common sounds.

nodes.title: Phonics
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can apply letter-sound correspondences to sound out unfamiliar single-syllable words.

nodes.title: Sight Words
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can instantly recognize and read grade-level high-frequency words without decoding.

nodes.title: Decoding
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can decode multisyllabic words by applying syllable patterns and blending.

nodes.title: Spelling
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can spell grade-level words correctly by applying phonics patterns, common spelling rules, and high-frequency word knowledge.

nodes.title: Fluency
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can read grade-level text aloud accurately, at an appropriate rate, and with expression.

nodes.title: Basic Comprehension
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can answer literal who/what/where/when questions about a text they have read.

nodes.title: Vocabulary
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can determine the meaning of grade-level words and use newly learned words accurately in speech and writing.

nodes.title: Context Clues
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can infer the meaning of an unknown word from surrounding context (definition, example, synonym, or contrast clues).

nodes.title: Roots & Affixes
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can determine a word's meaning by analyzing its root, prefix, and suffix.

nodes.title: Word Relationships
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can identify synonyms, antonyms, homophones, and complete simple word analogies.

nodes.title: Multiple-Meaning Words
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can distinguish among the meanings of a multiple-meaning word and choose the sense that fits the context.

nodes.title: Denotation & Connotation
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can distinguish a word's literal denotation from its positive, negative, or neutral connotation.

nodes.title: Idioms & Adages
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can interpret the figurative meaning of common idioms, adages, and proverbs.

nodes.title: Reference & Dictionary Skills
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can use a dictionary, glossary, or thesaurus to find a word's pronunciation, meaning, and part of speech.

nodes.title: Etymology & Word Origins
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can trace a word's origin across languages and use etymology to infer meaning and relationships.

nodes.title: Reading Comprehension
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can accurately restate what a grade-level text says and answer literal and simple inferential questions about it.

nodes.title: Reading Analysis
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can analyze how ideas, evidence, and structure in a text work together to convey meaning.

nodes.title: Main Ideas
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can identify the central idea of a passage and state it in their own words.

nodes.title: Supporting Details
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can locate the details in a text that support its main idea.

nodes.title: Inferences
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can draw a logical inference from a text and cite the evidence that supports it.

nodes.title: Cause and Effect
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can identify cause-and-effect relationships in a text and explain how one event leads to another.

nodes.title: Text Structures
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can identify a text's organizational structure (sequence, compare/contrast, cause/effect, problem/solution) and use it to aid comprehension.

nodes.title: Author's Purpose
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can determine whether an author writes to inform, persuade, or entertain and cite evidence for that purpose.

nodes.title: Summarizing
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can write a concise summary of a text that captures its main idea and key details without personal opinion.

nodes.title: Evaluate an Argument
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can evaluate the claims, evidence, and reasoning in a text and judge whether the argument is sound.

nodes.title: Fiction Elements
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can identify the characters, setting, and plot of a story and explain how they relate.

nodes.title: Point of View
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can identify the narrative point of view (first person, third-person limited, omniscient) and explain how it shapes a story.

nodes.title: Setting & Conflict
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can describe a story's setting and identify its central conflict (character vs. self, others, society, or nature).

nodes.title: Character Analysis
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can analyze a character's traits, motivations, and development using textual evidence.

nodes.title: Plot Structure
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can map a story's exposition, rising action, climax, falling action, and resolution.

nodes.title: Theme
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can state the theme of a literary work and support it with evidence from the text.

nodes.title: Literature (Intro)
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can retell a literary text and identify its genre and basic story elements.

nodes.title: Literary Analysis
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can analyze how literary elements and devices contribute to a work's meaning.

nodes.title: Advanced Literature
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can analyze complex literary works across genres, comparing themes and techniques among texts.

nodes.title: Mood & Tone
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can distinguish a text's mood from its tone and cite the word choices that create each.

nodes.title: Figurative Language
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can identify and interpret similes, metaphors, personification, and hyperbole in a text.

nodes.title: Literary Devices
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can identify literary devices such as symbolism, irony, foreshadowing, and allusion and explain their effect.

nodes.title: Genre Study
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can distinguish major genres (fiction, nonfiction, poetry, drama) by their defining features.

nodes.title: Drama & Theater
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can identify the elements of drama (acts, scenes, dialogue, stage directions) and interpret a play.

nodes.title: Literary Criticism
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can apply a critical lens (e.g., historical, feminist, formalist) to interpret a literary work.

nodes.title: Poetry Analysis
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can analyze how a poem's structure, sound devices, and figurative language create meaning.

nodes.title: Text Features
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can use text features (headings, captions, bold words, diagrams, index) to locate information and aid comprehension.

nodes.title: Critical Thinking
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can evaluate reasoning, detect bias and logical fallacies, and judge the credibility of a source.

nodes.title: Parts of Speech
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can identify the eight parts of speech and their function in a sentence.

nodes.title: Nouns & Pronouns
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can identify common, proper, singular, and plural nouns and the pronouns that replace them.

nodes.title: Verbs & Verbals
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can identify action, linking, and helping verbs and recognize verb forms in a sentence.

nodes.title: Adjectives & Adverbs
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can identify adjectives and adverbs and explain which word each modifies.

nodes.title: Conjunctions & Prepositions
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can identify prepositions, coordinating and subordinating conjunctions, and interjections and use them correctly.

nodes.title: Sentence Structure
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can construct complete grammatical sentences with a subject and a predicate.

nodes.title: Subject & Predicate
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can identify the complete subject and complete predicate of a sentence.

nodes.title: Sentence Types
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can identify and punctuate declarative, interrogative, imperative, and exclamatory sentences.

nodes.title: Simple, Compound & Complex Sentences
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can distinguish and produce simple, compound, and complex sentences.

nodes.title: Fragments & Run-ons
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can identify and correct sentence fragments and run-on sentences.

nodes.title: Clauses & Phrases
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can distinguish independent from dependent clauses and identify phrases within a sentence.

nodes.title: Grammar & Mechanics
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can apply grade-level grammar, usage, and mechanics conventions in their writing.

nodes.title: Subject-Verb Agreement
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can make verbs agree with their subjects in number, including with tricky subjects.

nodes.title: Pronoun Usage & Agreement
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can use pronouns correctly and make them agree with their antecedents in number and gender.

nodes.title: Verb Tense & Consistency
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can use verb tenses correctly and keep tense consistent within a piece of writing.

nodes.title: Commonly-Confused Words
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can correctly use commonly-confused words such as their/there/they're, your/you're, and its/it's.

nodes.title: Punctuation & Capitalization
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can apply grade-level rules for capitalization and end, internal, and quotation punctuation.

nodes.title: End Marks
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can end sentences with the correct period, question mark, or exclamation point.

nodes.title: Commas
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can use commas correctly in series, compound sentences, addresses, and after introductory elements.

nodes.title: Apostrophes
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can use apostrophes correctly for contractions and possessives.

nodes.title: Dialogue & Quotation Punctuation
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can punctuate dialogue and quotations correctly with quotation marks, commas, and end marks.

nodes.title: Capitalization
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can capitalize sentence beginnings, proper nouns, titles, and the pronoun I correctly.

nodes.title: Paragraph Writing
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can write a coherent paragraph with a topic sentence, supporting details, and a closing sentence.

nodes.title: Opinion Writing
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can write an opinion piece that states a preference, supplies reasons, and provides a concluding statement.

nodes.title: Multi-Paragraph Writing
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can organize a multi-paragraph composition with an introduction, body paragraphs, and a conclusion.

nodes.title: Essay Writing
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can write a focused essay with a clear thesis, developed body paragraphs, and transitions.

nodes.title: Textual Evidence
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can support a written claim by quoting or paraphrasing relevant textual evidence and explaining it.

nodes.title: Narrative Writing
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can write a narrative with a clear sequence of events, descriptive detail, and dialogue.

nodes.title: Informative Writing
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can write an informative text that introduces a topic, develops it with facts, and groups related information.

nodes.title: Writing Process
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can move a piece of writing through prewriting, drafting, revising, editing, and publishing.

nodes.title: Prewriting
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can generate and organize ideas before drafting using brainstorming, outlining, or graphic organizers.

nodes.title: Drafting
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can turn a prewriting plan into a complete first draft.

nodes.title: Revising
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can revise a draft to improve ideas, organization, word choice, and clarity.

nodes.title: Editing & Proofreading
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can edit a draft to correct grammar, spelling, punctuation, and mechanics errors.

nodes.title: Publishing
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can produce a clean, formatted final copy of a piece for an audience.

nodes.title: Creative Writing
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can craft an original creative piece using imagery, voice, and figurative language.

nodes.title: Advanced Creative Writing
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can develop sustained creative works with sophisticated structure, voice, and stylistic control.

nodes.title: Advanced Writing Styles
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can adapt style, tone, and structure across narrative, informative, and argumentative modes.

nodes.title: Research Basics
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can locate relevant sources, take notes, and avoid plagiarism while gathering information on a topic.

nodes.title: Research Writing
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can write a research paper that integrates and cites multiple sources around a controlling idea.

nodes.title: MLA & APA Citation
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can format in-text citations and a works-cited/references page in MLA and APA style.

nodes.title: Synthesis Writing
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can synthesize ideas from multiple sources into an original, well-supported argument.

nodes.title: Technical & Professional Writing
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can produce clear technical and professional documents (reports, proposals, instructions) for a defined audience.

nodes.title: Research Skills
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can plan and carry out an inquiry: pose a research question, evaluate sources, and synthesize findings.

nodes.title: Rhetoric (Persuasion)
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can use ethos, pathos, and logos to persuade an audience in speech or writing.

nodes.title: Argumentation & Debate
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can construct an argument with a claim, evidence, reasoning, and a rebuttal of counterclaims.

nodes.title: Claims & Counterclaims
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can distinguish a claim from a counterclaim and acknowledge and refute opposing views.

nodes.title: Evidence & Reasoning
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can select relevant evidence and explain the reasoning that links it to a claim.

nodes.title: Rhetorical Analysis
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can analyze how a writer's rhetorical choices achieve a purpose for a specific audience.

nodes.title: Formal Logic
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can evaluate deductive and inductive arguments and identify common logical fallacies.

nodes.title: Media Literacy
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can analyze messages across media, identifying purpose, technique, bias, and reliability.

nodes.title: Digital Communication
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can communicate effectively and responsibly across digital platforms for varied audiences.

nodes.title: Dialect
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can recognize regional and social dialects and explain how variety in language reflects audience and context.

nodes.title: Public Speaking
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can plan and deliver an organized oral presentation with appropriate volume, pace, and eye contact.

nodes.title: Active Listening & Discussion
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can listen attentively, build on others' ideas, and contribute relevant comments in a collaborative discussion.

nodes.title: Advanced Communication
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can adapt sophisticated verbal and nonverbal communication to varied audiences and high-stakes contexts.

nodes.title: Register (Formal & Informal)
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can choose an appropriate level of formality in language for a given audience, purpose, and situation.

merges.note: Overlap A1-1: E5 Basic Comprehension, L-007 Reading Comprehension, and E9 Reading Analysis are the SAME reading-comprehension strand at three levels. BOTH retained (each is a distinct english-lyceum game skill and student progress is keyed by title) and wired as the canonical spine E5 -> L-007 -> E9. No node removed; no cross_domain edges migrated.
Overlap A1-1 (cont.): E9 Reading Analysis retained as the top of the comprehension spine above L-007. E9's cross_domain edges (SS3/SS5/SS6/SS7/SS8/SS19/SS24 <-> E9, B2/B5 <-> E9) stay on E9.

Overlap A1-2: L-012/013/014/015 (Fiction/Character/Plot/Theme) duplicate the E21->E22->E23 Literature spine. E21->E22->E23 is the analytical spine; L-012 Fiction Elements and its atomics (L-013 Character, L-014 Plot, L-015 Theme, EN-204 Point of View, EN-207 Setting & Conflict) are retained as concrete atomics feeding E22. All are distinct game skills, so no node removed.

Overlap A1-3: L-018 Research Skills overlaps E14 Research Basics / E18 Research Writing. L-018 RETAINED (it is a distinct game skill, 'Research Skills') but subordinated above the research spine (hard_prereq E18; soft E14, L-017) and stage corrected Mastery -> Integration. Canonical spine: E14 -> E18 -> L-018.

Overlap A1-4: L-019 Critical Thinking overlaps E47 Formal Logic / E19 Argumentation / E44 Rhetorical Analysis. L-019 RETAINED (distinct game skill 'Critical Thinking') but subordinated as a capstone (hard_prereqs E9, E19; soft E47, E44, EN-220) and stage corrected Mastery -> Integration.
Overlap A1-5: L-011 Cause and Effect is a subset of E34 Text Structures. L-011 RETAINED as a concrete atomic (distinct game skill) with E34 added as a soft_dep. No node removed.
